known_degeneracies_that_must_be_labelled: For tap and scroll the release fake touch IS the victim own held recording transported to the carrier endpoints: rebuilding it from the five reproduces the released fake trajectory to float32 ulp (see release_touch_channel_is_a_replayed_five_shot_template). row4 - row2 is therefore near-tautological for those two actions and any null result there is guaranteed by construction, not measured.

For the same reason row 3 differs from row 5 in touch CONTENT only through the extra resample and re-clock the fake template already went through; a null row3 - row5 for tap/scroll is weak evidence about content.

coverage_declaration_F7.entitled_cells: the 20 classical imu_trajectory_xytime cells only (10 deep joint cells GPU-deferred).
coverage_declaration_F7.why_not_imu_only: the arms do not alter the inertial channel at all -- row 3 carries a genuine held recording IMU bit for bit and row 4 carries the release fake IMU bit for bit. An imu_only number would restate the genuine arm or the released fake arm and would say nothing about pairing.
coverage_declaration_F7.why_not_trajectory_only: the declared variable is the CROSS-CHANNEL pairing, which does not exist in a single-modality cell. On trajectory_xytime the arms would differ from the release only by which carrier supplied the row count and clock, which is a re-timing measurement, not a half-attack measurement.

mechanics.S0: CARRIER = the event supplying the inertial window; it fixes T = len(carrier imu) and D = carrier_trajectory[-1, 7] * 1000 ms (channel 7, never a row count, never an IMU length).
mechanics.S1: TEMPLATE = the event supplying the touch trajectory, resampled to T by the release own _resample_touch_template.
mechanics.S2: SECOND STAGE: endpoint replacement onto the CARRIER own first/last touch sample, run through the release own _observe_exact_touch_template (tap/scroll/swipe) with the release own _fiveshot_tap_drift_request endpoint policy for tap. Identity for pinch and keystroke -- see correction_2.
mechanics.S3: elapsed rewritten by detector_grid_clock(T, D); dx/dy recomputed from the resampled contact mask and coordinates.

correction_1_resample_rule.problem: _resample_touch_template returns early when source and target lengths match (replay_dataset_builder.py:1404), so the earlier max|delta| = 0 over 5,584 events only exercised the early-return path and proved nothing.
correction_1_resample_rule.what_was_done: the rule was characterised on genuinely DIFFERENT lengths only; every call in the probe has target != len(source).
correction_1_resample_rule.plain_statement: On differing lengths the rule is NOT interpolation of the path. Channels 0,1,2,3,4,8 (contact, x, y, pressure, pointer count, availability) are NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR HELD with index round(t*(n-1)) (verified exactly); only channel 7 (elapsed) is linearly interpolated; channels 5,6 (dx, dy) are RECOMPUTED from the resampled contact mask and coordinates, not resampled (1/40 events agree with a hold-resample of the source deltas). First and last rows are preserved. Upsampling duplicates 26.5% of consecutive rows on average. The map is lossy and only 71.8% of N->M->N round trips return the original x column (max round-trip error 0.154 in screen-relative units). It departs from a true linear interpolation of x by up to 0.059 relative.

correction_2_second_stage.problem: repair_joint() omitted the release second stage (endpoint replacement at replay_dataset_builder.py:2164 for tap/scroll/swipe and pinch area similarity at :1592), which would leave rows 3/4/5 with an uncontrolled screen-position shift relative to rows 1/2.
correction_2_second_stage.what_the_release_actually_does: the requested endpoints come from the attacker bound Android CARRIER target (_single_pointer_target_control_points_px, replay_dataset_builder.py:4615), NOT from the donor template. Measured over 120 released fake events per action for 3 test victims, the requested start sits a median 351-405 px away from the donor own start, so the second stage is a real spatial move.
correction_2_second_stage.decision: RESTORED for tap, scroll and swipe, by calling the release own _observe_exact_touch_template with the carrier own first/last touch sample as the requested control points -- the same semantics the release uses (carrier owns the endpoints).

not_restorable_for.pinch: the release pinch placement (_observe_pinch_area_similarity) needs frozen live two-pointer endpoint geometry (pinch_start_points_px / pinch_end_points_px / pinch_scale_direction) that only a genuine material row carries; a released FAKE pinch, which is row 3 touch donor, stores only the centroid and carries no such geometry.
not_restorable_for.keystroke: the release keystroke touch is not a transported template at all -- fiveshot_keystroke_rhythm_v1 composes it from key DOWN anchors taken from a replacement carrier plus the victim hold/flight rhythm, so there is no template-to-endpoint transport to reapply.

correction_2_second_stage.treatment_for_those_two: S2 is the IDENTITY, applied identically to rows 3, 4 and 5. Consequently, for pinch and keystroke rows 3/4 are compared ONLY against row 5 and never against rows 1/2.

release_touch_channel_is_a_replayed_five.why_this_matters: it decides what row 3 and row 4 can mean. If the released fake touch is itself a real held recording of the victim, then "fake touch" and "real touch from the five" are not two different contents and the contrast the experiment intends is not present in the release.

evidence.provenance: every released fake tap/scroll/swipe carries donor.role = exact_touch_template_generator and donor.source_material_cluster_id pointing at one of the victim own five published shots, with template_resampled_to_carrier = true; every released fake pinch carries role = fiveshot_pinch_area_similarity with the same kind of pointer; keystroke carries no material template.
evidence.bitwise: the lifecycle columns of the resampled material template (contact, pointer count, availability) and its pressure column are bitwise identical to the released fake for all four template-based actions (max abs diff 0.0 over 120 events per action).

release_touch_channel_is_a_replayed_five.plain_statement: Rebuilding the released fake touch from the victim five held recordings through S1+S2+S3 reproduces the released fake trajectory to float32 ulp for tap (max 6.0e-8 screen-relative) and scroll (max 3.0e-7), to a median 0.020 screen-relative for swipe, and not at all for pinch (identity S2 here vs a similarity in the release) or keystroke (different mechanism). So (a) the builder IS the release touch pipeline, byte for byte where the release path is reconstructable, and (b) for tap and scroll the release touch channel contains no synthetic geometry.
release_touch_channel_is_a_replayed_five.consequence_for_row4: row 4 for tap and scroll is the release arm re-derived with a re-drawn shot; row4 - row2 there is near-tautological (F14) and must be labelled where the number is stated.

parity_table_F3.action_composition: identical for rows 2, 3, 4 and 5: exactly 200 events per (victim, action) per repetition, 20 victims, 5 actions. Row 1 is the genuine pool and is not an arm under test (its per-action counts are 1042 tap / 2000 scroll / 2000 swipe / 1999 pinch / 1950 keystroke over the 20 test victims).
parity_table_F3.declared_variable: which channel is synthesised (and, for row 5, that neither is)
attributes_that_still_differ_and_why: resample ratio (carrier T / template T): after length-matching row 5, the mean log2 ratio is row3 0.140 vs row5 0.136 for scroll, 0.051 vs 0.063 for tap, -0.056 vs -0.073 for keystroke -- matched; but 0.099 vs 0.052 for swipe and 0.178 vs 0.124 for pinch. The residual gap of up to 0.054 in mean log2 (about 4 percent in length) is a DECLARED remaining parity defect: the victim genuine pool does not contain events short enough to match every fake template. Before-and-after is visible in the row5 vs row5_unmatched entries.

second stage residual scale: the release on-screen guard shrinks the transported residual on a minority of events. Sample medians are 1.000 in every arm; the minima differ (scroll row3 0.510, row4 0.133, row5 0.412), so the tail of this mechanic is not perfectly matched and should be carried into the scoring phase as a covariate.

orientation: the template and carrier orientation disagree on a small fraction of events in every arm (rates recorded above); the release itself mismatches donor and target orientation on 3.5-7.6 percent of its own fake events, so this is the release own behaviour rather than something introduced here.

confound_check_duration_and_T.question: do the arms differ in duration or T before anything is scored
confound_check_duration_and_T.plain_statement: row 3 and row 5 have IDENTICAL T and IDENTICAL duration event for event in all five actions (they share the carrier), and row 4 and row 2 have identical T and duration multisets (row 4 carriers are the whole release fake pool). Row 3 vs row 2, row 4 vs row 5 and row 5 vs row 2 are NOT matched -- e.g. scroll T p5 is 24.9 in row 3 against 19.0 in row 2, and keystroke median duration is 3815 ms in row 3/5 against 4400 ms in row 2/4. Any FAR difference on those three comparisons is duration-confounded.
confound_check_duration_and_T.recommendation_for_the_scoring_phase: report all five paired differences as asked, but lead on row3 - row5 and row4 - row2, and carry a duration-stratified version of the three confounded ones.
